name: Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Clavicle

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Clavicle

criteria.description: Presence of a painless, palpable mass or lump over the midshaft of the clavicle present since birth or early infancy
Radiographic evidence of a well-defined pseudoarthrosis with sclerotic bone ends and absence of callus formation
No history of clavicular fracture or trauma to explain the nonunion
Normal neurologic examination of the upper limb

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a painless palpable mass over the clavicle since birth with radiographic confirmation of pseudoarthrosis and absence of trauma history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by characteristic radiographic findings; genetic testing is not routinely required.

imaging: X-ray showing midshaft clavicular nonunion with sclerotic bone ends and absence of callus
CT scan for detailed bone anatomy if needed
MRI to exclude soft tissue or neurovascular involvement
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; usually sporadic
other: Physical exam revealing painless clavicular lump and shoulder asymmetry

distinguishingFeatures: Radiographic evidence of fracture healing or callus formation
Pain and tenderness at fracture site
Genetic testing positive for RUNX2 mutations

redFlags: Rapidly increasing swelling or pain over clavicle
Signs of neurovascular compromise in ipsilateral upper limb
Fever or systemic signs suggesting infection
references: Orphanet: Congenital pseudoarthrosis of the clavicle - ORPHA:66630
Kozin SH, et al. Congenital pseudoarthrosis of the clavicle. J Pediatr Orthop. 1991;11(3):355-360.
Bae DS, et al. Congenital pseudoarthrosis of the clavicle: diagnosis and treatment. J Am Acad Orthop Surg. 2006;14(7):388-395.
